A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching methods, experimental domains, and Appendices A–C. The text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original SVAR simulations, causal-discovery evaluations, and sortability analyses of competition, river-flow, and Causal Chamber data, including appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical analyses and reports additional causal-discovery benchmark scores in Tables 1 and 3.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same sorting, LASSO regression with BIC selection, and lagged-predecessor regression procedure. The corrected score formula does not establish a change to the implemented causal-discovery algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same ER-SVAR configurations, 14 competition dataset configurations, four river networks, and 17 Causal Chamber datasets. Additional F1 results concern existing coverage; all 215 experiment-level rows in Appendix C match.

E2.justification: The Causal Chamber comparison drops reversed varsortnregress from v1 Table 4 when incorporating the results into v3 Table 3. This comparator remains in the river experiment. The expanded comparisons otherwise use the existing PCMCI+, sorting, and random-regression methods.

E3.justification: The added competition F1 table specifies maximum lag 3, conflicting with the retained dataset-dependent 3–5 setting in Section 5.1. The expanded Causal Chamber evaluation specifies lag 2. Equation 6 also corrects the documented score normalization. These changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun under different settings.

E4.justification: The analyses of performance versus sortability and contemporaneous versus lagged recovery contain revised F1 distributions in v3 Figures 2–3, corresponding to v1 Figures 2–4. Their questions remain the same, and the four degree-sensitivity plots in Appendix B are identical.

E5.justification: Both versions use means with standard deviations and boxplots, retaining the stated 30 samples per sortability interval. Additional F1 entries extend existing reporting practices; no new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or statistical estimation procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: v3 adds competition F1 comparisons and expands Causal Chamber F1 reporting from two datasets to ten. For example, Table 1 newly reports FinalCLIM_N-5_T-100 scores of 0.51 ± 0.23 for varsortnregress and 0.40 ± 0.13 for PCMCI+. The main F1 boxplot values also change, and two reversed-varsortnregress scores disappear. River results and appendix results remain unchanged. The incomplete FinalWEATHnoise_N-10_T-1000 row in v3 Table 1 prevents reliable interpretation of its changed cells.

T1.justification: Equation 6 removes v1's extraneous sum over k from the denominator, correctly normalizing by the number of admissible pairs. Section 3 also corrects the reversed numerator/denominator description of cyclic pairs. These are localized mathematical corrections, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion narrow references to score-based algorithms to continuous score-based algorithms. The introduction and conclusion additionally emphasize that simple sorting benchmarks can match or outperform sophisticated methods on highly sortable data. The central contributions remain intact.

C2.justification: v3 explains missing Causal Chamber benchmark scores through insufficient samples or excessive runtime and interprets the additional comparisons as evidence of exploitable sortability. A new introduction sentence says river widths decrease downstream, contradicting the retained widening explanation in Section 6. The main limitations paragraph is unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 newly states that SVAR samples follow a burn-in period, discloses maximum lag 2 for Causal Chamber benchmarking, and explains exclusions involving insufficient samples or datasets exceeding 50,000 samples. These add implementation and reporting detail without establishing changes to the retained experiments.

R1.justification: v3 adds Hyvärinen et al. (2010) when introducing SVAR models and removes the Langbridge et al. (2023) citation and reference. The positioning relative to Reisach, Pamfil, and Ng remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The six main sections and three appendices retain their organization and much of their wording. Changes include short explanatory additions, expanded benchmark discussion, updated affiliations, acknowledgments, and removal of the separate supplementary-material title block.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column workshop layout to a single-column journal layout. v1 Figures 2 and 3 become paired panels in v3 Figure 2, and performance plots receive new styling and legends. Tables 1 and 3 expand substantially, the separate Causal Chamber benchmark table is absorbed into Table 3, and river-table columns are reordered.

improvement.justification: Correcting Equation 6 and broadening the competition and Causal Chamber comparisons improve mathematical clarity and empirical support beyond v1's limited benchmark reporting. The gains are qualified by new reporting problems: Table 1 contains an incomplete weather-data row, and Table 3 supports seven varsortnregress wins rather than the claimed nine out of ten. The useful additional evidence supports a modest net improvement.
